cards.title: Introduction to File Handling
cards.content:
File handling is an important part of any web or software application. Python has several functions for creating, reading, updating, and deleting files.

To open a file, Python uses the built-in open() function, which returns a file object.

options.text: r stands for read, w stands for write
r stands for remove, w stands for write
r stands for read, w stands for wait

cards.title: Reading from Files
cards.content:
To read a file in Python, use the read() method.

f = open("demofile.txt", "r")
print(f.read())

You can also return only one line by using the readline() method.

content.text: To open a file for reading, we use open("file.txt", "___")

cards.title: Writing and Appending to Files
cards.content:
To write to an existing file, you must specify a mode to the open() function:

  • "a" - Append - will append to the end of the file
  • "w" - Write - will overwrite any existing content
f = open("demofile.txt", "a")
f.write("Now the file has more content!")
f.close()

cards.title: Using the 'with' Statement
cards.content:
It is good practice to use the with statement when dealing with file objects. This creates a context manager that automatically closes the file when the nested block of code exits.

with open("demofile.txt", "r") as f:
    data = f.read()
    print(data)

cards.title: Order the Safe File Writing Steps

steps: Open the file using the with statement and write mode
Call the write() method with your string data
Let the context manager automatically close the file

cards.title: Deleting Files and Folders
cards.content:
To delete a file, you must import the OS module, and run its os.remove() function:

import os
os.remove("demofile.txt")

To delete an entire folder, use os.rmdir().
